title: Key takeaways: How AI and legal finance are changing patent monetization
summary: Key takeaways from a webcast discussing how AI and legal finance can help companies identify and unlock value in their patent portfolios. Learn more.
body_markdown:
In a recent webcast with Patlytics CEO and Co-Founder Paul Lee, we discussed how advances in AI, combined with legal finance, are making it easier for companies to identify and pursue that value.


[Watch the webcast: Unlocking Value from Corporate Patent Portfolios: Legal Finance and AI-Powered Patent Workflows in Practice](https://www.burfordcapital.com/insights-news-events/insights-research/webcast-patlytics-and-burford-patent-ai/)


Below are four key takeaways:


## 1. Patent monetization is moving into the corporate mainstream


Companies are becoming much more proactive about extracting value from their intellectual property.[Burford’s research found that 71% of in-house IP lawyers have already divested patent assets or are actively exploring divestiture](https://www.burfordcapital.com/insights-news-events/insights-research/2025-patent-monetization-survey/) .


That shift is also visible in Burford’s deal flow. Increasingly, patent finance opportunities are coming directly from operating companies rather than exclusively through law firms. Companies are considering a wider range of strategies, from divestiture to licensing and litigation, depending on the assets and their broader business objectives.


## 2. AI can turn portfolio analysis from a bottleneck into an opportunity


For companies with hundreds or thousands of patents, simply identifying which assets merit closer attention has traditionally required significant time and resources.


AI-powered tools can dramatically accelerate that first stage of analysis. During the webcast, Patlytics explained how companies can analyze portfolios for potential infringement and validity issues, identify promising assets and narrow a large portfolio to a manageable subset for deeper review.


At Burford, we increasingly see companies bring us opportunities where this initial work has already been performed, creating a much more focused starting point for conversations about licensing, direct enforcement or divestiture.


## 3. Identifying a strong patent is only the beginning


AI can help identify promising assets, but a strong infringement analysis does not automatically make a patent an attractive monetization or financing opportunity.


Companies still need to consider validity, potential damages, commercial considerations, and existing licenses. Those factors can influence whether the appropriate path is licensing, litigation, divestiture—or waiting until market conditions make an asset more valuable.


The question is therefore not simply “Which patents look strong?” but *“Which strategy creates the most value from these patent assets?”*


## 4. AI accelerates judgment; it does not replace it


Perhaps the most important takeaway is that AI remains a tool rather than a substitute for expert judgment.


AI can eliminate substantial amounts of manual analysis and help companies, counsel and finance providers reach the most relevant questions much faster. But lawyers and other experts still need to validate the analysis and assess the legal, financial and commercial context.


As AI makes sophisticated portfolio analysis faster and more accessible, the opportunity for companies is broader than efficiency alone. Combined with legal expertise and appropriately structured capital, it can help transform patents from largely passive assets into a more actively managed source of strategic and financial value.
